A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same research work and complete Appendices A–I. Text comparison and rendered-page inspection establish corresponding text, equations, figures and tables without material reading gaps.

before.justification: Section 4 and Appendices B–C report original reinforcement-learning experiments, including benchmark comparisons, Bottleneck investigations and component ablations.

after.justification: The original experimental results and learning curves remain in Section 4 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: Equations (5)–(9), observe/optimize switching, Algorithm 1 and the known-monitor variant in B.5 are unchanged. The G.4 modification concerns a proof definition, not the algorithm.

E1.justification: Both retain the same 48 benchmark combinations and Bottleneck experiments, including stochastic and never-observable rewards, different monitors and known-monitor scenarios.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged: Directed-E2 remains the main baseline, with Optimistic MBIE-EB and Pessimistic MBIE-EB retained in the corresponding Figure 12–13 ablations.

E3.justification: Both retain discount factor 0.99, evaluation every 100 training steps over 100 test episodes, the same episode limits and observability settings, and unchanged Table 1 hyperparameters.

E4.justification: The visitation analysis, stochastic-observability and known-monitor studies, and optimism/pessimism ablations retain the same questions and evidence in Figures 5 and 9–13.

E5.justification: Both report 30 seeds or trials and 95% confidence intervals for the experimental results. No repeated-run information or uncertainty-reporting practice changes.

E6.justification: The plotted results and empirical findings match, including outperformance on 43 of 48 benchmarks, similar performance on the remaining five, and the reported 30% reduction in steps with a known monitor.

T1.justification: Section 2.2 changes the infinitely-often observation condition from positive probability to probability one. Appendix G.4 removes both immediate-reward estimates and the discount multiplier from its auxiliary value definition and adds an all-states quantifier. These are localized mathematical revisions; Theorem 3.1 and the subsequent derivation remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: Monitored MBIE-EB, empirical exploration advantages, exploitation of known monitors, and finite-sample minimax-optimality guarantees.

C2.justification: Interpretations of pessimism, reward observability and known-monitor benefits are unchanged. Section 5 retains the limitations concerning separate objectives, explicit counts and enumerable spaces, and stopping-rule design.

D1.justification: Both retain the pseudocode, value-iteration budget, Newton-solver settings, hyperparameters, CPU/runtime disclosures and code-access information. No implementation details are added or substantively revised.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are unchanged, including the relationships to Mon-MDPs, Directed-E2, MBIE-EB and partially observable reward frameworks.

P1.justification: Edits mainly replace internal 'Appendix' references with 'Section' and adjust punctuation. Some references regress: B.3 and B.5 incorrectly point to Footnote 2, and several lemma/corollary references become 'Theorem.' Narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Small equation-spacing and text/footnote reflows alter layout, notably on pages 6–8. Figures 1–13, the notation table, Table 1 and algorithm displays retain their designs and placement.

improvement.justification: The probability-one correction in Section 2.2 is helpful. However, G.4 removes reward and discount terms while the unchanged argument before Equation (24) still treats the auxiliary quantity as a full value function, weakening proof consistency. Incorrect footnote and theorem references also reduce traceability. These limited regressions outweigh the clarification; the method and empirical evidence remain unchanged.
